title: Kinetic energy (গতিশক্তি)
placement: Book page 104, topic 4.3.1: ৪.৩.১ গতিশক্তি (Kinetic Energy). Next to the derivation W = Fs = … = ½mv² and the boxed formula T = ½mv², with the sentence on v being squared and the result ½mv² = ½mu² + W.
description: Interactive 3D indoor archery range for textbook topic 4.3.1 (page 104), in a school sports hall (maple floor, padded brick walls, an arrow-stop net). A realistic archer draws a red recurve bow: the bent bow stores energy; on release the string pushes the arrow (it does work on it), the arrow flies (shown 15 times slower) and sinks into a straw boss with a 60 cm target face, cut open to show how deep. Tap steppers pick the arrow's mass m (0.02, 0.03, 0.04 kg: carbon, aluminium and wooden arrows) and speed v (20 to 60 m/s; a heavier arrow cannot be drawn as fast by this bow), and the student shoots by the big action button, a tap on the archer, or by dragging the string back and letting go. The panel fills in the book's formula T = ½mv² with their numbers in J, compares each shot with the one before (twice the speed: four times the kinetic energy and about four times as deep; twice the mass: twice), and states the book's rule. Physics: an ideal linear bow (K = 400 N/m, 200 N at a 0.5 m draw) giving all its stored energy to the arrow, real gravity drop, and a steady straw resistance of 160 N (depth = T / F). Five scene-based test questions. Archer, bow, arrows and bale export as GLB. Offline, Bangla and English.
